instruction: Re-establish the tab that was previously closed in the browser.

metadata.explanation: Task requires agent to reopen the last closed tab (linkedin.com) using Ctrl+Shift+T. Evaluator verifies all 3 social media websites are present in open tabs.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator uses is_expected_tabs which checks both tab presence AND order via are_lists_equal
Instruction only requires 're-establishing' the closed tab, not maintaining specific tab order
Browser behavior for Ctrl+Shift+T is non-deterministic - reopened tab position varies by browser version and settings
The reopened linkedin tab could appear at position 2 (original), position 3 (end), or as active tab in different order
Order-sensitive comparison creates false negatives when tab is successfully reopened but in different position
Expected values are semantically correct (all 3 URLs should be present)
Core verification logic works but is over-constrained
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change evaluator to use set-based comparison instead of list equality (check tab presence, not order)
Use a custom metric that verifies all expected URLs exist in open tabs regardless of order
Alternative: Update expected value structure to indicate order doesn't matter
Or: Add postconfig to verify tab order if order is actually important to the task
